authorSelfScore.scorer: author self-score (the authoring agent; not the independent score create-rigged-character-assets requires)
gaps: The case is still lighter than the sheet's near-black mahogany (about sRGB 99, 60, 43 against 66, 38, 29 on the back panels), because the dielectric wood's specular adds grey under the shared light rig.

The glazed doors read as an even amber pane over a faint glowing disc; the sheet's frosted glass has a bright orange core glow. The interior glow stays peach at the project's GLOW_STRENGTH 0.7 convention for F08C2C, and the phase-2 corona reads as glowing gear teeth without bloom, short of the sheet's blazing escapement.

Limb armour (layered pauldrons, gunmetal upper arms with brass strips, squared vambraces, narrow thigh plates, greaves, knee bosses, sabatons with lames) carries gunmetal edge piping, but at the compare's scale the plates read smooth; the brass is uniform polished, without the sheet's engraving.

From the side the head reads as a smooth helm with no visible face-plate profile or eye glow; the arms hang in the frontal plane, so the anchors sit edge-on behind the legs where the sheet shows them angled forward.
The sabatons are smaller and darker from the front than the sheet's broad brass sabatons.
Phase change: the side plates stay shut until 0.85 s and spring open by 1.0 s; during those 0.15 s they sweep through the upper arms before settling behind them. The end pose is clear.
authorSelfScore.method: Author self-score from grand-escapement.fidelity-compare.jpg: orthographic EEVEE renders (AgX, the fixed shared light rig, not tuned to the score) of the low-poly model at the concept sheet's front, side and back angles, framed at the sheet's own scale (3.2 m over 808 sheet pixels), judged side by side and in zoomed crops of the head and bell, pediment, glazed doors, pauldrons, arms and anchors, legs and sabatons, plus the seven in-engine clip shots in staging/engine (three.js 0.186.1, ANGLE Metal on Apple M4). Case width and depth, pediment and roof heights, door and apron heights, head and bell sizes, hip, knee and ankle positions, the head's forward offset (side view: head bounding-box centre 0.067 m ahead of the case centre on the sheet, about 0.06 m on the model), and anchor spans were measured on the sheet's front and side views at the same framing. The case follows the sheet's squat cabinet rather than the design notes' longcase, because the sheet is the concept under review. Case colour was matched by sampling: the sheet's back panels read about sRGB (66, 38, 29); the model's back panels read about (135, 88, 65) before this pass and about (99, 60, 43) after it (darker, more saturated mahogany albedo and wood roughness 0.85, checked in both the Blender compare and the engine shots).

independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the model)

rubric.note: Geometry is unchanged since the score of 77, so this holds at 25. The boxy case and pediment on long brass legs, the long arms with anchors and the bell crown match the sheet. The shoulders are bulbous spheres rather than layered pauldrons, the case reads slightly tall and narrow, and in the side view the arms hang in the frontal plane with the anchors edge-on behind the legs where the sheet angles them forward.

Up 1. In phase 1 the escapement wheel and pendulum bob now read as an amber light source through the glass instead of a flat pane, and the eyes glow amber (about sRGB 229, 163, 67). Phase 2 now plays in the game: the guardian-vault log shows 'opens its case: phase 2' and the doors and side plates open on the same skeleton. Still short: the eyes are round goggle rings rather than the art bible's slits, the glass is clear rather than frosted, and the wheel is a flat emissive disc with thin spokes laid over it rather than the sheet's brass toothed wheel with a blazing rim.

Unchanged at 13, since the geometry and materials are the same. The case mouldings, door frames and brass trims read well, and the glass is transparent in the engine. The brass limbs are smooth with no engraving, and the case wood has little painted value variation.

Up 1. With the case open, the core measures about sRGB (246, 183, 66), hue 35-39 and saturation 0.70, against the sheet's blazing wheel at (243, 159, 65), hue 32 and saturation 0.72. That is slightly yellower than the sheet but matches the art bible's candle amber F3BE65. Still off in three ways. Through the closed doors the core washes to about (230, 175, 100) at saturation 0.56, against the sheet's (234, 154, 65) at 0.73. A salmon corona ring around the disc, about (215, 142, 102) at hue 22, still covers roughly a third of the glow area (about 3,100 px against 6,300 amber px), and the sheet has almost no pixels in that band. The case wood reads about (89-114, 63-73, 51-55) against the sheet's near-black mahogany at (64-71, 36-41, 30-31).

Up 1. In the engine shots at the seated 2.6 m distance, the amber core is now the brightest and most saturated element of the case in both phases, and the open case, anchors and silhouette are unmistakable. The closed-door core is still small and washed out behind the glass. The desktop game camera crops the head and most of the case off the top of the frame, which is camera framing, not the model, and is not scored.

topFixes: Finish the glow pass: recolour the salmon corona ring around the escapement disc to the same amber, and frost or tint the door glass so the closed-door core reads as saturated orange (sheet about sRGB 234, 154, 65) rather than a pale (230, 175, 100) wash. Make the wheel itself a brass toothed rim lit from behind, not a flat emissive disc.
Replace the round goggle eyes with amber eye slits on a face plate that reads from the front and the side.
Darken the case toward the sheet's near-black mahogany (about sRGB 66, 38, 29), and replace the sphere shoulders with layered, engraved pauldrons.
independentScore.method: Independent visual review against assets-source/concepts/escapement-sheet-1.png and docs/art-bible.md by a separate reviewer agent, using the same rubric as the previous score of 77 (silhouette and proportions 30, signature features 25, surface detail and material read 20, colour and value 15, readability at play distance 10). The new in-engine shots after the glow fix ab14b81 were judged: p6-glow-grand-escapement.jpg (closed), p6-glow-grand-escapement-open.jpg (phase-2 open) and the grand-escapement row of p6-glow-before-after.jpg. Glow colour was measured with Pillow as sRGB medians over HSV masks (amber core: hue 30-50, saturation above 0.6, value above 0.85; salmon ring: hue 8-28, saturation 0.3-0.62) and compared with the same masks on the sheet's panel 1, panel 3 and front doors. The game shots p6-guardian-phase-opening.jpg and p6-guardian-phase-open.jpg were committed in 2990e46, before the glow fix, and measure peach (about 202, 128, 90, hue 20), so they were used only as evidence that phase 2 plays in the game, not for colour. Geometry was judged from the unchanged fidelity compare, review sheet and model-low front and three-quarter renders, and pose readability from the older engine phase-change-end clip. Silhouette and surface were held at their previous points because the geometry is unchanged. This object replaces the previous score of 77, which had been written nested inside authorSelfScore and is now at top level, matching bellows-golem.
